11 Conduct of Operations

This chapter of the Preliminary Safety Analysis Report (PSAR) describes the preliminary plan
for the applicant’s organization, training of personnel, conduct of operations, and coping with
emergencies that are required by 10 CFR 50.34(a)(6) and (10) to be included in the construction
permit (CP) application. This chapter also provides information related to the technical
qualifications of the applicant to engage in the activities discussed in the application pursuant to
10 CFR 50.34(a)(9). Also included in this chapter is a description of the construction fitness-for-
duty (FFD) program required by 10 CFR 26.401(b).

This chapter is structured as follows:

Organization - Section 11.1

Concept of Operations - Section 11.2
Training - Section 11.3

Emergency Planning - Section 11.4
Procedures - Section 11.5

Security and FFD - Section 11.6

The information in this chapter is informed by the Advanced Reactor Content of Application
Project (ARCAP) interim staff guidance - for example, DANU-ISG-2022-01, “Review of Risk-
Informed, Technology-inclusive Advanced Reactor Applications — Roadmap,” and
DANU-ISG-2022-05, “Advanced Reactor Content of Application Project Chapter 11,
‘Organization and Human-System Considerations,” - that the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) has issued to support the development and review of a CP application
PSAR for an advanced non-light-water reactor (non-LWR). However, the human factors
engineering program considerations recommended in the NRC ARCAP guidance for PSAR
Chapter 11 are described in PSAR Section 8.7 and evaluated in SE section 8.7. As the DANU-
ISG-2022-05 review criterion evaluates the Organization, Concept of Operations, Training and
Procedures together, Section 11.1 of this SE incorporated the staffs review of SE Sections
11.2, 11.3, and 11.5 together.

11.1 Organization
Section 11.1 of the PSAR describes the applicant’s organizational structure and key
management positions in the organizations that are responsible for facility design, design

review, design approval, construction management, testing, and plant operation.

The applicable regulatory requirements for the evaluation of the design, construction, and
operating organizations are as follows:

e 10 CFR 50.34(a), which describes the minimum information to be included in a
preliminary safety analysis report and requires, in part, the following:

e 10 CFR 26.3(c), which requires, in part, that construction permit holders shall comply

11.1.1 Technical Evaluation

The NRC staff evaluated section 11.1 of the PSAR using the guidance and criteria of DANU-
ISG-2022-05. In addition, this section of the SE incorporates the NRC staff's review of PSAR
sections 11.2, 11.3, and 11.5.

11.1.1.1 Assignment of plant operating responsibilities

DANU-ISG-2022-05 criterion 11.2(a) states that the applicant should describe the assignment of
plant operating responsibilities, the reporting chain up through the chief executive officer of the
applicant, the proposed size of the regular plant staff, the functions and responsibilities of each
major plant staff group, the proposed shift crew complement for single-module/-unit or multiple-
module/-unit operation, and the qualification requirements for key members of the plant staff.

 OPFICIALLUSE-ON-LY—_PRORRIETARYINEORMAHON

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 11.1.1, which describes the functions and responsibilities
of each major plant staff group that will be established in support of construction and pre-
operational testing activities. The reporting chain up through the chief executive officer is
depicted in Figure 11.1-1, “Project Organization,” including, in part, Engineering Design,
Procurement and Supply Chain, Technology Development, and Program Director reporting to
the Senior Vice President of Commercial Operations. The Senior Vice President of Commercial
Operations reports to the President, along with the Quality Assurance Manager and
Environmental Health and Safety.

With specific regard to operations staffing, PSAR section 11.2.3 states that the requirements of
10 CFR 50.54(m) will be addressed at the operating license (OL) application stage. The NRC
staff notes that the specifics of the shift crew complement that will be utilized during plant
operations is an area for which review may reasonably be deferred until the future review of an
OL application. The NRC staff further notes that, although the proposed size of the regular plant
staff is not described in numerical terms, the PSAR references the NRC approved “Xe-100
Licensing Topical Report Control Room Staffing Analysis Methodology” (ML23258A243), which
will be used to develop the staffing plan described in the application for an OL. The descriptions
of the organizational structure, reporting relationships, and functions across the organization
provide an appropriate degree of detail for the CP application review stage, as discussed in
DANU-ISG-2022-05, and that the review of further details regarding operating organization
composition can also reasonably be deferred until the review of an OL application. The NRC
staff therefore concludes that the applicant has adequately described plant operating
responsibilities, reporting relationships, organizational structure, functional areas, and
qualifications to the degree appropriate for a PSAR, consistent with criterion 11.2(a) presented
in DANU-ISG-2022-05.

11.1.1.2. Technical qualification of applicant

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(b) states, in part, that the applicant should be technically
qualified. The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 11.1 which states that Long Mott Energy, LLC
(LME), along with X Energy, LLC (X-energy), is responsible for the design and construction of
the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS). LME is a wholly owned subsidiary of GWN Holding,
LLC, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Dow Chemical Company (TDCC). TDCC is
described as a large multi-national petrochemical company that safely operates more than 50
gas and steam turbines at 30 sites worldwide. TDCC is also described as having expertise and
experience in design and construction management of large-scale projects. TDCC and LME
have an inter-company agreement to procure technical and financial support, including
personnel, to ensure that the requisite leadership, engineering, procurement and administrative
assistance is available for completion of the design and construction of LUGS. The PSAR
further states that TDCC partnered with NextEra Energy Resources, LLC (NEER), a subsidiary
of NextEra Energy, the largest electric utility in the United States, including the operation of
seven light water reactors at four sites, to provide technical support to LME in areas including,
but not limited to, nuclear procurement, licensing activities, personnel training, and operating
discipline development.

Based upon the technical experience available through X-energy, TDCC, and NEER, the NRC
staff concludes that the applicant is technically qualified to undertake construction of LMGS,
consistent with criterion 11.2(b) presented in DANU-ISG-2022-05.

11.1.1.3. Key positions for ensuring the safe operation of the plant

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(c) states that the applicant should describe the key positions
for ensuring the safe operation of the plant within the operating organization, consistent with the
quality assurance program (QAP) and ANSI/ANS 3.2, as well as the capability for on shift
personnel to provide initial facility response in the event of an emergency.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.2.2, which discusses the responsibilities of the
Executive Vice President and Chief Nuclear Officer, who has overall responsibility for plant
nuclear safety and implementation of the QAP.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.2.3, which states that, during the operational
phase, the Plant General Manager “assures the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of the
plant within the constraints of applicable regulatory requirements, the operating license, and the
QAP.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Figure 11.1-3 “Operating Organization,” which provides an
overview of the proposed operating organization, including an Emergency Response
Organization (ERO) under the Operations Coordinator. The staff also reviewed PSAR section
11.4.3, which states that the composition, structure, and staffing of the ERO will be developed
based on an analysis of the emergency response functions needed to respond to emergencies
and will be submitted as part of an OL application.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 12.1.1.4, which discusses the LMGS organizational plan
to include construction, commissioning, and operations teams for project execution. The NRC
staff notes that the PSAR does not describe whether the operating organization will comply
either with the organizational provisions of ANSI/ANS 3.2 or with an alternative approach.
However, given that this criterion specifically addresses the facility organization during the
operating phase, the NRC staff determined that the complete evaluation of this criterion,
including any related commitment to ANSI/ANS 3.2, can reasonably be deferred until the review
of an OL application.

11.1.1.4 Initial test program and technical support

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(d) states, in part, that the applicant should adequately
describe the groups and key positions responsible for implementing the initial test program
(consistent with the quality assurance program and ANSI/ANS 3.2) and for providing technical
support for the operation of the facility.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 12.1.1.4, which states, in part, that the commissioning
schedule, in support of the initial test program, will include control room operators, plant field
technicians, and other technical, engineering, and operational support personnel. Operational
support personnel will include chemistry and radiation protection technicians. Additionally, the
PSAR further states that vendor technical field advisors and third-party contracted resources will
be available for providing support for their respective systems, structures, and components
(SSCs) or discipline area.

The NRC staff notes that ANSI/ANS 3.2 addresses the operational phase of plant life, which is
entered prior to initial fuel loading. As such, the NRC staff determined that evaluation of the
consistency of the test organization with either ANSI/ANS 3.2 or an alternative approach can

reasonably be deferred until the future review of an OL application. The NRC staff therefore
concludes that the applicant has described the organization responsible for implementation of
the initial test program, the related QAP considerations, and the organizational provisions for the
technical support of facility operations, consistent with criterion 11.2(d) presented in DANU-ISG-
2022-05.

11.1.1.5 Plans for the construction, testing, and operating organizations

DANU-ISG-2022-05 criterion 11.2(e) states that the applicant should describe plans for the
construction, testing, and operating organizations that are consistent with the relevant portions
of NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, "Management and Technical Support Organization" and
sections 13.1.2 - 13.1.3, "Operating Organization.” The NRC staff considered the guidance
within these documents against the information otherwise addressed by the criteria of DANU-
ISG-2022-05, as well as within the context of a CP application/PSAR review and identified
specific criteria of NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1 that were of relevance. These criteria are
evaluated within sections 11.1.1.5.1 through 11.1.1.5.6 of this SE.

11.1.1.5.1 Integrated management of activities

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion III.1(a)(ii) states that the applicant should describe how
the organization provides for the integrated management of activities that support the
construction, operation, and maintenance of the facility.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1, which discusses the integration of organizational
management at the executive level and states that the management “establishes expectations
for quality, safety, and efficiency in plant operations and support activities.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR section 11.1.1.1, which states that the “President is responsible
for all aspects of design and construction.” This section describes that design and construction
responsibilities are assigned to the executive responsible for project execution, with control of
nuclear plant operation subsequently being assigned to the Chief Nuclear Officer prior to pre-
operational testing. PSAR section 11.1.1.8 discusses that the quality assurance manager
reports to the President and is responsible for quality assurance, quality control, and the
implementation of the LME Quality Assurance Program Description (QAPD) (ML20343A088).

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.2, which states that the Senior Vice President of
Commercial Operations is “responsible for the administration of reactor development, nuclear
licensing, and support activities for LME under the [QAPD].” This position is responsible for
ensuring that LME programs, products, and processes deliver the highest technical quality and
nuclear safety for the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of nuclear plants.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.9, which states that the “Program Construction
Manager is responsible for the construction activities of the full PLM [Project Long Mott]
Program and reports to the Program Director.” This position’s responsibilities include, among
others, environmental, health, safety and security, quality, subcontract management, cost and
schedule performance and control, as well as overall management of the physical project site
and temporary facilities.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.11, which states that the lines of authority,
decision-making, and communication are clearly and unambiguously established between the

project members, including contractors. Additionally, the section further states that “no later
than six months prior to fuel receipt of the unit, those positions that are identified for operations
will be staffed and will be given the appropriate authority required to perform operations
activities.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Figure 11.1.-2, “Construction Organization” and Figure 11.1-3,
“Operating Organization,” which graphically describe the organizational structure for
management of construction, operation, and maintenance activities consistent with the sections
of the PSAR reviewed above.

The NRC staff therefore concludes that the applicant has described how the organization
structure will provide for integrated management of construction, operation, and maintenance
activities, consistent with Criterion IlI.1(a)(ii) presented in NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1.

11.1.1.5.2 Obtaining personnel

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion III.1(a)(iii) states that the applicant should describe how it
will obtain personnel with sufficient experience to provide management and technical support for
the facility.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.2.3 which describes that LME is leveraging a process
for selection of an Engineering, Procurement, Construction management (EPCm) contractor for
the LMGS. The process, with processes to include a solicit, evaluate, and award the contract, is
performed by a multifunctional team including LME, X-energy, TDCC, third party nuclear
construction and engineering experts, and the intended operator.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.7 which states that the Program Director reports
to the President during the construction phase and is responsible for site-related construction
activities. The NRC staff notes that the QAPD addresses the qualifications of personnel in
technical and management roles. The NRC staff therefore concludes that the PSAR describes
how staffing will be obtained to support construction of the facility and that further evaluation of
acquiring personnel for the operating organization can be deferred until the review of an OL
application.

11.1.1.5.3 Control of major contractors

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion III.1(a)(vii) states that the applicant should describe how
the organization will carry out its responsibilities to control major contractors and has committed
to consider safety first, with due consideration of risk insights, in design and construction of the
facility and during the transition from construction through testing to operation.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.2 which describes that the Senior Vice President
of Commercial Operations will be responsible for ensuring quality and nuclear safety. PSAR
section 11.1.1.3 describes that the Environmental, Health and Safety (EH&S) reports to the
President and has the “authority and responsibility to ensure that safety standards are
incorporated in all aspects of the activities associated with LMGS.” PSAR Section 11.1.1.3 also
states that the “EH&S has the authority to stop work when unsafe behaviors or results are
observed.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 8.1.4 which states that the LMGS Reliability Assurance
Program will be implemented using the QAP during construction phase activities. It further
states that programmatic controls, including organizational controls, design controls, procedures
and instructions, corrective action process, records, audits, and expert panels, are established
to assure that risk insights are identified, maintained, and communicated to the responsible
organizations.

The NRC staff therefore concludes that the applicant has described how the organization will,
beginning in the design and construction phases and continuing through testing to operation,
control major contractors while incorporating consideration of both safety and risk, consistent
with Criterion III.1(a)(vii) presented in NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1.

11.1.1.5.4 Safety responsibility

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion III.1(b) states that the applicant should identify the
corporate officer responsible for nuclear activities and a commitment by the applicant that this
individual will have no ancillary responsibilities that might detract attention from nuclear safety
matters.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.2 which describes that the Senior Vice President
of Commercial Operations is responsible for ensuring quality and nuclear safety.

The NRC staff therefore concludes that the corporate officer responsible for nuclear activities
and safety matters is identified within the application, consistent with Criterion III.1(b) presented
in NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1.

11.1.1.5.5 Construction responsibilities

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion III.1(c) states that the applicant should define the design
and construction responsibilities for applicant and vendor personnel, both in terms of numbers
of personnel and necessary position qualifications and experience.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.9, which states that the Construction Program
Management reports to the Program Director and is responsible for all construction activities.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.1.10, which describes the role of the Primary
Scope Area Construction Managers, whose responsibilities include oversight of construction
activities within their designated work assignments in areas including quality and technical
compliance with specifications, compliance with health and safety standards, schedule
adherence and documentation management for commissioning.

Additionally, the NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.2.8, which discusses the
responsibilities of the Security Manager, who provides guidance and direction to the Plant
General Manager on the site surrounding nuclear security, access authorization, and fitness for
duty programs, as well as the responsibilities of the Training Manager, who is responsible “for
the development, implementation, and maintenance of training to construction personnel.”

The NRC staff therefore conclude that the PSAR adequately defines applicant and vendor
responsibilities for design and construction, as well as key personnel roles and qualifications

 OPFICIALLUSE-ON-LY—_PRORRIETARYINEORMAHON

associated with construction, consistent with Criterion III.1(c) presented in NUREG-0800 section
13.1.1.

11.1.1.5.6 Responsibilities for human factors engineering

NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion IIl.1(d) states that the applicant should clearly define
management and organizational responsibilities to address human factors engineering (HFE)
considerations.

The NRC staff notes that PSAR section 8.7 addresses the HFE considerations for the LMGS.
For NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1, Criterion IIl.1(d), the NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 8.7.2,
which states that the PLM HFE program is developed under the LME Quality Assurance
Program. It further states that the requirements of the HFE program “flow down to suppliers and
potential sub-suppliers via procurement documents.” Oversight of the suppliers and sub-
suppliers is performed in accordance with the QA program.

The staff therefore concludes that management and organizational responsibilities are clearly
defined as they relate to the addressing of HFE considerations, consistent with Criterion III.1(d)
presented in NUREG-0800 section 13.1.1.

11.1.1.6 Plans for conduct of operations

DANU-ISG-2022-05, Criterion 11.2(f) states that the applicant should describe plans for the
conduct of operations that are consistent with the relevant portions of NUREG-0800 sections
13.5.1.1, "Administrative Procedures — General” and 13.5.2.1, "Emergency and Operating
Procedures."

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.5 which describes the LMGS plan for developing,
implementing, and maintaining plant procedures including: (1) Administrative procedures for
plant operations, (2) Operating procedures, which includes normal operating, abnormal,
emergency, and alarm response procedures, and (3) Maintenance and other procedures, which
includes test, surveillance, chemistry and radiation protection procedures. This section of the
PSAR further states that the three procedures groups listed above are developed using the
applicable guidance of ANSI/ANS-3.2-2012, that was endorsed in RG 1.33 to meet the
requirements of 10 CFR Part 50, Appendix B. The PSAR also states that the procedures are to
be “developed and implemented in a sufficient time frame before fuel load to permit plant staff
familiarization and to facilitate regulatory review.” The staff notes that the applicant did not
specify in PSAR Section 8.7.2 the applicable principles and practices that will be used to
develop the associated procedures as part of the HFE program, along with the other HFE
elements found in NUREG-0711. This area is discussed in Section 8.7.3.3 of this SE. The staff
therefore concludes that review of the applicant’s plans for the conduct of operations can
reasonably be deferred until the review of a future OL application.

11.1.1.7 Education and experience requirements for key personnel

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(g) states that the applicant should propose education and
experience requirements for key personnel that conform to the qualifications and experience

 OPFICIALLUSE-ON-LY—_PRORRIETARYINEORMAHON

guidance endorsed by RG 1.8, “Qualification and Training of Personnel for Nuclear Power
Plants.” The staff notes that RG 1.8, endorses ANSI/ANS 3.1, “Selection, Qualification, and
Training of Personnel for Nuclear Power Plants.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.3.2 which states that the licensed operator training
program will include requirements for minimum education and experience of trainees, as
determined in coordination of the Systems Approach to Training (SAT) program development.
The PSAR further states that these requirements will be submitted for approval as part of the
training program for licensed operators and will “provide reasonable assurance that licensed
operators are trained and qualified... to operate and maintain the plant in a safe manner.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.3.3 of the PSAR, which describes the training
programs for non-licensed personnel. The PSAR states that RG 1.8 and ANSI/ANS-3.1, with
exceptions and clarifications, will be reviewed for applicability and suitability for LMGS plant staff
positions when determining education and experience requirements. The PSAR describes that
development of the minimum requirements will be determined systematically in accordance with
SAT training program development. The PSAR further states that these minimum requirements
will “provide reasonable assurance that licensed operators are trained and qualified with
sufficient knowledge and skill to operate and maintain the plant in a safe manner during all
modes and conditions of operation.” These requirements will be submitted for approval as part
of the training programs for non-licensed operators.

The staff therefore concludes that the PSAR addresses education and experience requirements
for key personnel that are consistent with the guidance of RG 1.8, and consistent with Criterion
11.2(g) presented in DANU-ISG-2022-05.

11.1.1.8 Proposed operating organization

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(h) states that an applicant’s proposed organization should
conform to the guidance of RG 1.33 or the applicant has provided justification for an alternative.
The staff notes that RG 1.33 endorses ANSI/ANS 3.2.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.1.2.3, which provides a description of the duties of
Plant General Manager. Included in those responsibilities are the development of the site
operating and support staff, and for operation of the new nuclear plant during all test phases.
During the transition to operating phase activities, this position “assures the safe, reliable, and
efficient operation of the plant within the constraints of applicable regulatory requirements, the
operating license, and the QAP.”

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 12.1.1.4, which states that the LMGS organizational
arrangement allows a division of resources into clear construction, commissioning, and
operations teams for each module. Section 12.1.1.6 of the PSAR describes the turnover
process from construction to cold commissioning, with formal turnover packages of all
construction activities that include inspections, analyses, and acceptance or performance
criteria.

The staff notes that the PSAR does not describe whether the Operating Organization will
comply with the organizational provisions of ANSI/ANS 3.2 or with an alternative approach.
However, given that this criterion specifically addresses the facility organization during the

operating phase, the staff concludes that the evaluation of this criterion, including any related
commitment to ANSI/ANS 3.2, can reasonably be deferred until the review of an OL application.

11.1.1.9 Compliance with minimum staffing requirements

DANU-ISG-2022-05 Criterion 11.2(i) states that an applicant should describe how an adequate
number of licensed operators will be available at all required times to satisfy the minimum
staffing requirements of 10 CFR 50.54(m), or else provide justification for an exemption.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.2.3 which states that LME plans to perform a staffing
optimization analysis, using the HFE program developed in accordance with NUREG-0711,
“Human Factors Engineering Program Review Model”, Revision 3 (ML12324A013), to
determine the number of licensed operators as well as the qualifications of control room and
supporting personnel. The PSAR further states that LME anticipates that the final staffing
analysis is expected to confirm an optimum control room staffing level of three licensed
operators (i.¢., one shift supervisor and two control room operators) controlling four reactor
modules from a single control room. PSAR section 11.2.3 acknowledges that the staffing level
and configuration does not meet the requirements of 10 CFR 50.54(m). However, the staff notes
that PSAR section 11.2.3 states that a staffing optimization analysis will be conducted
consistent with NUREG-1791, “Guidance for Assessing Exemption Requests from the Nuclear
Power Plant Licensed Operator Staffing Requirements Specified in 10 CFR 50.54(m)”
(ML052080125), and that the applicant intends to provide sufficient justification for an exemption
of 10 CFR 50.54(m), which will be submitted as part of the OL application.

The staff therefore concludes that the applicant has described preliminary plans for licensed
operator staffing to the extent warranted for a PSAR consistent with Criterion 11.2(i) presented
in DANU-ISG-2022-05, and that further review of compliance with the staffing requirements at
the OL stage, including the planned exemption request, comply with 10 CFR 50.54(m) and
NUREG-1791

11.1.1.10 Engineering expertise on shift

DANU-ISG-2022-05, Criterion 11.2(j) states that the applicant should describe how engineering
expertise on shift will be consistent with the Commission Policy Statement on Engineering
Expertise on Shift (50 FR 43621) and within the guidelines of Three-Mile Island (TMI) Action
Plan Item 1.A.1.1, “Shift Technical Advisor,” of NUREG-0737, “Clarification of TMI Action Plan
Requirements” (November 1980), or else provide justification for an alternative.

The NRC staff reviewed PSAR Section 11.3.3 which states that the Shift Technical Advisor
(STA) role “will be evaluated to determine if the role is necessary for the safe operation of the
LMGS during emergency conditions.” It further states that the guidance of SECY-21-0039,
“Elimination of the Shift Technical Advisor for the NuScale Design,” (ML21060A823) will be
considered and, if necessary, an exemption request with justification of the exemption
determination will be submitted as part of any future OL application.

The staff therefore concludes that the technical justification for the training or omission of the
STA, will be reviewed at the OL stage to ensure compliance with 10 CFR 50.120(b)(2)(iii) or 10
CFR 50.12.

11.1.1.11 Role and function of vendors during design and construction

DANU-ISG-2022-05, Criterion 11.2(k) states that the applicant should describe the role and
